alternative: Known difference between the models compared: Think-SFT's single samples are noisier per problem than RL's (mean pairwise inter-sample Pearson r of 0/1 scores 0.42 vs RL 0.52 at matched ~93% accuracy). Any single-sample arm with RL's own per-problem consistency (an independent RL draw, or anything with RL-like sampling noise) correlates with RL's 4-sample rate at the Spearman-Brown ceiling sqrt(4)*r1/sqrt(1+3*r1), which sits above Think-SFT's single-sample correlations. So a positive D2 follows from Think-SFT's extra sampling noise plus the noisy one-sample edit correlation. It does not need the edit to carry RL's mechanism. Accuracy can't be the explanation: edit 0.94 vs Think-SFT 0.93. Length (+0.026) and cap-hit covariates explain less.
computation: 1) Problems: pids present in all three cells (edit row; RL attempt 0 samples 0-3; Think-SFT attempt 0 samples 0-3). 2) rate_RL(p) = mean score_v3 of RL attempt-0 samples 0-3. 3) r1 = mean over the 6 pairs (a<b) of RL samples 0-3 of Pearson r(score_v3 of RL sample a, score_v3 of RL sample b) across problems. 4) clone = 2*r1/sqrt(1+3*r1), the expected Pearson r of one independent RL-like sample with the 4-sample RL rate. 5) ct = (1/4)*sum_s Pearson r(Think-SFT sample s score_v3, rate_RL), s=0..3. 6) Alternative value = clone - ct.
